posts.name: Nepycros
posts.cooked:
Mint acquired.

 

I used every power I had to give Tachyon the chance to experiment on the Sentinels. I missed a LOT (which is surprising considering they have the highest statistics of successful experiments out of anyone else in the game), but being able to play several Sentinels cards per round meant I could whittle away at the Ennead. Argent Adept played support by buffing the damage from Idealist and Writhe, which was the bulk of my splash damage.

posts.name: Yoshi348
posts.cooked:
Mint.

Basic plan was triple Blocks plus Human Shield to be utterly invincible, pretty much. The rest of the team lays out enough ongoings/equipment naturally to weather the Ancient Magicks without losing your key cards. I experimented on Tachyon rather than the Sentinels, and I feel like it paid off in her big burst-fueled cards. Really, though, this team is ridiculous. Pretty much your only real problem is if you accidently End of Days yourself.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
Yoshi348:

…I experimented on Tachyon rather than the Sentinels, and I feel like it paid off in her big burst-fueled cards. Really, though, this team is ridiculous…

Played a practice match to get the feel of it, and yep, this team is ridiculous; the combination possibilities are endless.  Re: Experiment, 32 out of the 40 cards (80%) in the Sentinels deck are one-shots, so Experimenting on them with SS Tachyon is about as guaranteed a double-card-play as you're going to get.  With the potential to use Experiment 3-4 times a round to fish for Team Communication and Unique Capabilities, you can get out all of their Signatures/Ongoings in no time flat.  

 

UPDATE:  Mint.  The God of Random Seeding was against me, so Experiment didn't work as well on the Sentinels' deck as it did on my practice game, but still no sweat.  Once Human Shield and Sentinels Tactics are out, the Ennead's piddly little instances of 1-3 AOE damage can't hurt the heroes, and all you need to watch out for are Ancient Magicks and Mass Overheating. 

 

P.S.  This team was so ridiculously fun that I used them to take on Challenge Mode Spite and then Challenge Mode Voss.  Again, once Human Shield and Sentinels Tactics came out, neither of them had a chance.  Spite couldn't do any damage, so his Challenge condition (allowing him to heal beyond his base HP) was essentially a nullity.  As for Voss, he has a plethora of minions that all do various kinds of 2-3 AOE damage, so after taking a few hits, the heroes were essentially invulnerable from him.  Flipped him once and then kept killing his minions keeping him from ever flipping again, making his Challenge condition (playing an additional card when he flips) also useless.

posts.name: KateWalker
posts.cooked:
Guh.

Mint, but maybe it was the one-shot's title getting my hopes up. For a team with this much out-of-turn power usage and card play, I felt like everyone was super-useless. And it's all Fanatic's fault, because she never missed an opportunity to flip End of Days and wipe out all the heroes' stuff, while doing diddly squat to the villains.

It also didn't help that the first experiment on the Sentinels -- y'know, the thing that the one-shot seems to suggest you ought to do -- failed. And then Tachyon got one off on herself before that failed. And it failed on Legacy. And Fanatic. And Argent Adept. It wasn't until the Sentinels shuffled their trash into their deck that I got another Experiment to work, and then it was just one.

As far as I'm concerned, it was the team's healing potential, not anything else, that got me through this game. There's just nothing like watching all your Signatures get armageddon'd away twice in a row...

posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

I did what the despcription suggested, and experimented on the Sentinels every chance I got. Between Tachyon, Legacy and Fanatic, that was 3 experiments every round. Sometimes it didn't work, but I'd guess the experiments were successful 3 out of 4 times.

 

Wow, did it pay off! I had Argent Adept use the Bell to give damage boosts to various Sentinels (always the Idealist) via Syncopated Onslaught. With the addition of Sentinel Tactics, The Idealist turned into a MONSTER. She was practically my sole damage dealer, taking out Egyptian Gods left and right with her ninja robots and positive attitude. Fanatic did a bit of damage, too--primarily with Sacrosanct Martyr.

 

HP at end:  Medico 13, Writhe 14, Idealist 6, Mainstay 13, Tachyon 24, Legacy 23, Fanatic 10, Arget Adept 20.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Easy Mint with the Sentinels all near max, Fanatic at 14, and everyone else over 20. And that was with Tachyon hitting herself to keep Pushing the Limits out. Mainstay was the star of the show - Human Shield + Sentinel Tactics + Block + passing Idealist powers + Block meant that I could continually nullify just about all the Ennead's damage. Y'know, until Human Shield was destroyed on the last round, but hey, it was the last round.

I had a rough time Experimenting on the Sentinels as well - I missed three out of five attempts. It's all in what you choose in that first turn, apparently, when you get a deck shuffle after playing Unique Capabilities. Or not playing Unique Capabilities, I suppose.  I went with the Durasteel Chains, which promptly got nuked a turn later by the Ennead anyway.

I also had Fanatic play End of Days off the top of her deck, but I thankfully had AA able to pass her a card play to use Consecrated Ground to destroy it before it went off. 

After having issues with Experimenting on the Sentinels, I did Tachyon instead to MUCH better effect. She landed three 16+ Lightspeed Barrages and two Sonic Vortexes that hit everything on the board. The Ennead did get Set out, but that was all. Also, I got good use out of Sacrosanct Martyr + Smite the Transgressor - that let Fanatic do 10 damage to one Ennead on her final turn (2, then use base power, then max out SM to deal 8).
